mutations.name: Responses: the original defect — processChunk stops consulting `finished`, so response.failed is followed by output_text.delta
Anthropic: the original defect — processChunk stops consulting `messageStopped`, so a second content block opens after the error
Gemini: the original defect — processChunk stops consulting `finished`, so array mode appends a frame after the closing bracket and the body stops parsing
Anthropic: the guard reads the WRONG flag — sawTerminalSignal is set by the error branch itself, so the guard can never fire on a later chunk

SURVIVOR (documented): Gemini writeFrame drops its writableEnded check. Harmless because it is the SECOND of two gates on the same write path and the first now holds: processChunk returns on `finished`, so nothing reaches writeFrame after a terminal event, and writableEnded only differs from `finished` when the socket closed under us — which end() already makes a no-op. Measured: with this mutation applied the suite stays 26/0, i.e. no post-terminal write becomes reachable. It is NOT dead code — it is what stops a write to an aborted socket on the CLIENT-disconnect path, which no fixture here drives. If the processChunk guard is ever removed, this mutation must be re-run: it would then become the only gate.
OVER-REACH CONTROL: the guard fires unconditionally, so ordinary content never streams at all
